title: connect two onnx models as one
body:
Hi, supposely i have two onnx models and i want to combine both of them to get the mean of the two output, how should i do?
 for example:
x=onnx.load("x.onnx")
y=onnx.load("y.onnx")

i want to have one onnx model which give the same result as x+y

thanks for any help

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I think there’s utilities in this repo that will allow you to do that. 

@participant3 on a side note, this makes me think when we create the high level IR, we can have some APIs loaded to the IR object that allow us  to compose graphs intuitively like we are doing math. E.g. `graph1 | graph 2`

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
There are some utilities in `onnx.compose` in this repository that could help, like `onnx.compose.merge_models` - you'd need to prepare a third model which computes a mean of its inputs and then that could work.

I can also recommend a solution using [Spox](https://github.com/Quantco/spox). First you'll have to find all the input/output types of the models. Then you can use `spox.inline` to put the two models in the same model. With `spox.argument` you can create placeholder model inputs that you can forward the composed model inputs with. Then you can compute a mean (like arithmetic mean).

```py
import numpy as np
import onnx
import onnx.compose
import <redacted-host>.onnx.v17 as op
from spox import argument, build, inline, Tensor

# I'll assume your model inputs are some tensors a, b of these types
# You can adapt this to your case
a = argument(Tensor(int, (256, 256, 3)))
b = argument(Tensor(np.float32, ('N',)))

# Load the models
model1 = onnx.load("out/model1.onnx")
model2 = onnx.load("out/model2.onnx")

# Inline the models and forward the arguments
# Also unwrap all the results - here assume there's just one
(r1,) = inline(model1)(a, b).values()
(r2,) = inline(model2)(a, b).values()

# Take the arithmetic mean
# This assumes the outputs are float32 (as op.constant(value_float=...) is)
r = op.div(op.add(r1, r2), op.constant(value_float=2))  

# Build the composed model with given model inputs and outputs (with names)
model = build({'first': a, 'second': b}, {'result': r})
# onnx.save(model, ...)
```

I hope you can work out a solution based on this, but let me know if I can help further (or if you have more details on the models, like what input/output types they have).

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Something like this should work, depending on what are the exact model input/outputs:

```py
# Load model_1 and model_2
...

from spox import argument, Tensor, inline, build

column_names = ['col1', 'col2', 'col3', 'col4', 'col5', 'col6', 'col7', 'col8']

# Create a mapping of all the input columns, from strings to spox Vars (variables)
inputs = {name: argument(Tensor(str, (None,))) for name in column_names}

# Pass columns (inputs) by name with keyword arguments
(pred,) = inline(model_1)(**inputs).values()

# pred is a new Var that represents the output of model_1 
# - you want to pass it to model_2 now with another inline

# Pass pred as the sole argument to model2
(output,) = inline(model_2)(pred).values()

# output is a Var representing the output of model2 given model1's output

combined = build(inputs, {'output': output})
# combined is the resulting onnx.ModelProto
```

---

This attempt: 

```py
inline(model_1)([(x, argument(Tensor(str, (None,1)))) for x in columns]).values()
``` 
doesn't work because you are passing a list of pairs `tuple[str, Var]`. The format is either with positional or keyword arguments (`*args: Var` or `**kwargs: Var` - the keyword names are the column names). The above example passes by keyword arguments by doing `**inputs` on a `dict[str, Var]`.
I also wanted to add that `Tensor(str, (None, 1))` is a type of matrix `str[?][1]` where the second dimension is 1, not a vector `str[?]`. I assume you meant `Tensor(str, (None,))` here, which is a vector rather than a matrix, but you can correct it (Spox should raise if you use the wrong type).

This error:
```py
TypeError: inline callback missing required arguments: {'col1', 'col2', 'col3', 'col4', 'col5', 'col6', 'col7', 'col8'}, signature ['col1', 'col2', 'col3', 'col4', 'col5', 'col6', 'col7', 'col8'] (defaults ['shape_tensor']) -> ['variable'].
```
indicates the model expected arguments named `['col1', 'col2', 'col3', 'col4', 'col5', 'col6', 'col7', 'col8']`, and you haven't passed any of them (there's also a message that the output is called `'variable'`). I assume you must have used a call like `inline(model_1)()` for that exact error to be raised, unless there's a bug in the message.

> Model 1 output (and also model 2 input) will be 1400 columns of type float 64
I'm doing inline something like this - `(r2,) = inline(model_2)(argument(Tensor(float, (None,1400)))).values()`

I will note that the type `Tensor(float, (None, 1400))` represents a matrix of float64 `?` by `1400`, so `float64[?][1400]`. I assume that is what you meant to say, rather than 1400 separate columns?
Also, I want to note you shouldn't create a new `argument` here. That would indicate the input of `model_2` and the output of `model_1` are distinct. Instead, you should pass the `Var` returned from `model_1`.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
I've discovered the source of the bug. The 'adapting' mechanism in Spox ensures that opset versions are consistent across all used operators when they are built. In this case, inlining also has support for this, and as your models had versions `11` and `15` adapting was performed. As it turns out, in that specific code path there is a bug which leads to renaming not being performed correctly in a version-converted model. There are two possible workarounds:

1. Perform version conversion yourself, to avoid Spox's adapting to kick in. As far as I see, you can do this with `model_1 = onnx.version_converter.convert_version(model_1, 15)` before you `inline`. This is done because your first model is at version 11, and the second is at version 15. Note that this call will print the `'ai.onnx.ml'` warnings from ONNX, which I'm fixing in [this PR](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/pull/5103). 
2. The above workaround with performing a manual renaming yourself also helps: `build(**{"__" + k: v for k, v in inputs.items()}, {'output': output})` (this line prefixes all model input names with `__`)

I will try and get a Spox fix ready for this specific case in the next version. Inlining is still a bit wonky as it's really tricky to 'normalise' arbitrary ONNX models, and is done on a best-effort basis.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@participant4 Thank you for your feedback using Spox. Apologies, but I did not have much free time to look into your issue.

It looks like your non-spox model is using `ZipMap`, which I have not seen used before in a model, as support of the `map` type in ONNX is extremely limited. Because of this, I had not implemented the type in Spox. This causes attempts to `inline` the model fails as it cannot de-serialize the output type (`ValueError: Cannot get Type from invalid protobuf (not tensor, sequence or optional)`). I'll open a PR in Spox to add `Map`, as it's a small change, but as far as I see support in ONNX itself is buggy and other exceptions are raised in e.g. shape inference. I'll also try to look into the source of this, but it will probably only be fixed in the next ONNX release cycle. 

---

Your best bet is to remove usage of `map` entirely. As I see from your `producer_name`, you are using `skl2onnx`. Consider following [this guide](http://onnx.ai/sklearn-onnx/auto_examples/plot_convert_zipmap.html) (I am not familiar with the inner workings of `skl2onnx` myself) to remove the `ZipMap` from the model. This should also cause the output format to be closer to what you might expect.

An alternative approach from going through `skl2onnx` is to remove the `ZipMap` node yourself from the raw `non_spox.onnx` model you have and use the value called `probabilities` as the output. 

```py
import onnx

non = onnx.load('non_spox.onnx')
non.graph.node.pop(-5)  # Remove the 'ZipMap' node - I found it manually by looking at the node list
non.graph.output.pop(-1)  # Remove the output map - 'output_probability'
# Add the probabilities as an input instead
prob_type = onnx.helper.make_tensor_type_proto(onnx.TensorProto.FLOAT, (None, 2))
prob_info = onnx.helper.make_value_info('probabilities', prob_type)
non.graph.output.append(prob_info)
onnx.save(non, 'non_spox_no_map.onnx')
```

Now you will have an `? x 2` tensor in the second output called `probabilities`. To extract only the probabilities, you can add in the [`Gather`](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/main/docs/Operators.md#gather) operator to select index `1` across axis `1`. You can do this manipulating the ONNX directly, or in Spox:

```py
import onnx, spox
import <redacted-host>.onnx.v17 as op  # Import Spox's opset module for the default ai.onnx domain

# The input names in your model
names = ['publisher_id', 'device_model', 'device_type', 'banner_size', 'creative_id', 'adomain', 'creative_type', 'bundle']
args = {name: spox.argument(spox.Tensor(str, (None, 1))) for _ in range(8) for name in names}
xprob = spox.inline(onnx.load('non_spox_no_map.onnx'))(*args.values())['probabilities']
prob = op.gather(xprob, op.const([1]), axis=1)  # Apply the Gather operator here
model = spox.build(args, {'prob': prob})
onnx.save(model, 'non_spox_fmt.onnx')
```

This seems to result in the same output format as you have in your other example - a `? x 1` tensor of probabilities.
